title: Architect receives a 'small change' email that quietly becomes uncompensated additional service
job: Respond quickly to the client while preserving scope, fee and relationship.
trigger: Client, contractor or consultant requests work that may sit outside contracted scope.
surfaceComplaint: The project is busy and somehow the fee is gone.
mechanism: Scope boundaries live in contracts while new requests arrive in communication channels. Recognition often happens only after labor is spent.

actors.incentive: get desired outcome with low friction
keep client happy and protect margin

economics.painCostNote: Repeated small scope decisions can compound into tens of thousands in unrecovered labor.

buyer.roiLogic: One recovered additional-service event can repay the product.

distribution.acquisition: Integrate at request arrival, not month-end.

experiment.artifactRequest: contracts + client comms + timesheets + fee changes
experiment.success: find 3 credible missed moments worth >US$5k total and >70% PM agreement on live flags
experiment.kill: scope too ambiguous or flags create more relationship friction than value

claims.text: AIA identifies profitability and fee negotiation as major architecture-firm concerns for 2026.
Live request-to-contract comparison attacks leakage earlier than timesheet analytics.
